summary: Aiko Okoshi specialized in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She completed doctoral coursework at Kyoto University around 1970–1975 and served as a full-time lecturer at Kindai University in 1990.

Aileen Dansken Ross was an Indologist. She earned a B.Sc. from the London School of Economics and an M.A. and Ph.D. from the University of Chicago. She lectured at the University of Toronto before joining McGill University, becoming Professor in 1964.

Ajahn Amaro is a Buddhist studies scholar and monastic. He studied at Bedford College and trained under Ajahn Chah and Ajahn Sumedho. He co-abboted Abhayagiri Buddhist Monastery from around 1996 to 2010 and became Abbot of Amaravati Buddhist Monastery in 2010.

Ajahn Brahm specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the University of Cambridge and Emmanuel College, training under Boonman Poonyathiro and Ajahn Chah. He became abbot of Bodhinyana Monastery around 1983.
Ajahn Khemadhammo is active in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Drama Centre London from around 1963 to 1966 and trained under the traditional teacher Ajahn Chah around 1972–1977.
Ajahn Pasanno specializes in Buddhist studies. He trained under Ajahn Chah from around 1974 to 1982 and served as the founding co-abbot of Abhayagiri Buddhist Monastery from around 1996 to 2018.

Ajahn Sucitto focuses on Buddhist and religious studies. He completed a degree at the University of Warwick around 1968–1971 and trained under Ajahn Sumedho in 1977. He served as abbot of Chithurst Buddhist Monastery from 1992 to 2014.

Ajahn Sumedho studied at the University of California, Berkeley, and the University of Washington, and trained under Ajahn Chah. A scholar of Buddhism and religion, he served as abbot of Wat Pa Nanachat and Amaravati Buddhist Monastery.

Ajay Verma specializes in philosophy and Indology. He completed an M.Phil. and Ph.D. at the University of Delhi between 1997 and 2004, and became an Associate Professor at Jawaharlal Nehru University in 2005.
Ajit Ranjan Bhattacharyya was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied under Vidhushekhara Bhattacharya and held a post as an Ex-Puranchand Nahar Fellow at the University of Calcutta.
Akhil Rajeev P works in the fields of computational studies and Indology. He has held positions at the Centre for Development of Advanced Computing and the Indian Heritage Language Computing Group.

Akifumi Naito, a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar, studied at Ryukoku University, Honganji Sōgakuin, and under Gadjin Nagao. He held posts at Shinshu Institute of Doctrinal Studies, Ryukoku University, Kyoto Women's University, and Gyoshin Buddhist Academy.

Akihiko Akamatsu, an Indologist and philosopher, studied at Kyoto University under Yuichi Kajiyama and earned a Ph.D. at the University of Paris/Sorbonne Nouvelle. He held faculty posts at Kyushu University and Kyoto University, becoming Professor in 2001.
Akihiro Oda is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University. He held positions at Otani University, including full-time lecturer in 1992 and Professor of Buddhist Studies in 2013.
Akiko Kikuchi specializes in Buddhist studies and other fields. She studied as a research student at Minobusan University and became a Professor at Musashino University in 2022.
Akiko Murakawa is an Indologist. She studied under supervisors Harry Falk, Gerhard Ehlers, Masato Fujii, and Muneo Tokunaga, as well as teachers Werner Knobl, Yasuke Ikari, and Kazuhiko Yoshida.

Akiko Walley is a scholar of Japanology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Aoyama Gakuin University and Harvard University, and held a post at the University of Oregon from 2009 to 2016.

Akimichi Eda works in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned a Dr. phil. from the University of Marburg under doctoral supervisor Michael Hahn, and also studied under Katsumi Mimaki and Tsultrim Kelsang Khangkar.
Akio Donohashi works in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Tokyo from around 1968 to 1976 and served as a Professor at Kobe University from 1990 to 1991.

Akio Minoura is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He was an associate professor at Otani University (attested 2007–2013), conducted research abroad at Stanford University (2012–2013), and is affiliated with the Otani Academic Society.
